A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 29-page versions of LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately, including Appendices A–H. Text extraction, rendered-page comparison and inspection of plotted data support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original hidden-state clustering, steering, jailbreak, Latent Guard and adversarial-finetuning experiments in Sections 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical experiments, including the classification results in Tables 3, 8 and 9 and the reply-inversion results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The difference-in-means directions, activation-addition interventions and belief-based Latent Guard classifier retain identical procedures, including the steering-token rules in Appendix E.1.

E1.justification: AdvBench, JBB, Sorry-Bench, ALPACA, XSTest, CATQA, ToxicChat and OpenAI Moderation coverage is unchanged, as are the jailbreak, reply-inversion and adversarial-finetuning scenarios.

E2.justification: Llama Guard 3 remains the safeguard comparator in Tables 3, 8 and 9. The corresponding steering experiments retain the same harmfulness, refusal and reverse-direction comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported models, sampling, metrics, intervention procedures and finetuning settings are unchanged. Figure 12's revised axis labels do not add evaluated layers; both versions plot the same 32 layer positions.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2's layer-wise reply-inversion analysis revises one Llama3 outcome: Figure 12b no longer shows a strong reverse-harmfulness effect at layer 0. The other prompt, token-position, risk-category and finetuning analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting and uncertainty displays are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: In Figure 12b, reverse-harmfulness steering on harmful instructions changes from 76% refusal at layer 0 in v3 to 0% in v4. That curve's maximum consequently becomes 44% at layer 6. All other plotted data points, tables and textual findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of cluster scores, harmfulness/refusal beliefs and steering directions in Equations 2–5 are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about separate harmfulness/refusal representations, causal steering, jailbreak mechanisms and Latent Guard's effectiveness and finetuning robustness.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the narrow finetuning-attack qualification, limits on generalization beyond 7B/8B models and Appendix H.1's distribution-shift explanation. Figure 12's numerical revision receives no new discussion.

D1.justification: Hardware, sampling details, prompting templates, steering implementation information and code-access instructions are unchanged. The code-link destination is also identical.

R1.justification: Section 6, the reference list and positioning relative to prior refusal-direction, harmfulness-representation and jailbreak research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3, dated 8 October 2025, to v4, dated 14 December 2025. The prose, terminology, headings and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 12 replaces crowded, rotated layer labels with horizontal ticks at five-layer intervals, slightly reducing the space beneath its plots. Its legend and caption wording remain unchanged; other figures, tables and layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: Figure 12's clearer axes improve readability, but v4 also changes its strongest reverse-harmfulness result: layer 0 falls from 76% to 0%, leaving a maximum of 44%. Neither the experimental description nor discussion explains this revision. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the supporting evidence became more reliable, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
